source_review.notes: Checked all twelve references for identity, edition or version, date, and scope. The official IT Revolution record confirms Team Topologies second edition publication on 2025-09-23, authors, ISBNs, and retained focus on fast flow, cognitive load, four team types, and three interaction patterns. Official maintained Team Topologies key-concept and interaction-modeling pages were checked 2026-09-06. Checked primary or publisher records for Sweller, Conway, Parnas, SPACE, DevEx, CNCF Platforms, Accelerate, Bass-Clements-Kazman, and ISO 42010. The official ISO record lists ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2022 edition 2 as published. Practitioner constructs and cognitive-load transfer to teams are labeled as models, not universal empirical laws.

evidence: Defined team set, operational-context set, time window, five-dimensional demand and capacity vectors, and the six-field interaction tuple before use.
Checked componentwise inequalities, vector entries, averages, thresholds, and mode values for consistent scope and explicitly rejected unjustified vector addition.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The model represents bounded evidence about teams and contexts, not people as interchangeable capacity units.

evidence: Executed interaction-mode-heuristic under Python 3.14.4 and observed the exact four expected classifications with empty standard error.
Recomputed the counterexample average as (0+10)/2=5 against capacity average 6 and Exercise 2 average as 26/5=5.2 while identifying component breaches 7>6 and 9>6.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All numeric thresholds in the classifier are declared hypothetical.

evidence: Verified that componentwise acceptance L_j<=K_j for every j is stronger than an average inequality.
Confirmed the two-dimensional counterexample satisfies the average condition while violating one required component inequality.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The proposition denies scalar compensation only under the stated componentwise acceptability rule.

evidence: Reviewed missing and excessive capability, unstable contracts, permanent collaboration, shadow execution, legacy complexity, platform queues, shared policy, specialist succession, and delayed transfer.
Reviewed metric gaming, on-call harm, one-team-per-service fragmentation, giant platforms, clinical devices, and federated rail responsibilities.

evidence: Traced vector-capacity, interaction-lifecycle, and complexity-transfer invariants through selection, transition, operation, and review.
Confirmed platform, specialist, enabling, and stream responsibilities retain explicit outcomes, evidence, support, lifecycle, and non-responsibilities.
invariant_checking.notes: Every temporary mode has review or exit evidence and every service mode retains feedback and escalation.

evidence: Reviewed the non-compensation proof for stated componentwise premise, equal-weight average arithmetic, and valid counterexample conclusion.
Confirmed the proof establishes insufficiency of one average only, not the correctness of the five chosen dimensions or capacities.
proof_review.notes: The interaction classifier is explicitly a heuristic and is not treated as a theorem.

evidence: Audited uses of fundamental, model, proof, heuristic, viable, capacity, platform, owner, independent, safe, fast, and validated.
Confirmed team types are practitioner responsibility patterns, cognitive-load transfer is an analogy, and diagrams or labels are denied causal force.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Model, mechanism, implementation, policy, empirical evidence, and professional judgment remain distinct.

evidence: Executed the sole practical snippet with the repository verifier under CPython 3.14.4 on the recorded macOS environment.
Confirmed lending, checkout, actuarial, security, medical-device, and rail situations are hypothetical worked examples rather than field studies.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Local execution proves only the finite branch behavior in the recorded environment.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed flow mapping, stream alignment, multidimensional cognitive demand, platform product, complicated subsystem, enabling capability transfer, three interaction modes, team APIs, fracture planes, system-wide obligations, evolution, and humane measurement as one coherent architectural treatment distinct from SARCH-081 and Platform Engineering.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed failure and implementation paths across component queues, platforms, legacy systems, specialist engines, schemas, releases, on-call, security, data, conformance, handover, support, recovery, regulated devices, and federated transport. The chapter supplies actionable topology, interaction, exit, evidence, and transition practices. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified graduate and professional depth, exact four-type and three-mode distinctions, one multidimensional capacity model, three invariants, one proof and one executable heuristic, eighteen misconceptions, ten distinct worked examples, and five progressive exercises with complete answers ending in unfamiliar federated rail transfer.

limitations: Internal authoring, source, mathematical, executable-snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external organization-design, cognitive-science, labor, security, safety, accessibility, regulatory, platform, architecture, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The framework, vectors, heuristic, examples, and local execution do not establish an optimal topology, causal productivity, individual capacity, worker consent, regulatory compliance, system safety, or deployment fitness.
